feasibility.verdict: Feasible as an idealized single-column sensitivity experiment in ELM by cloning one site and overriding only the soil clay fraction (%clay) in the surface/soil dataset while holding forcing, PFT, topography, and all other parameters fixed.
answerable: How surface runoff vs. drainage (recharge) partitioning of infiltrating water shifts as clay content increases from 5% to 55%
How saturated hydraulic conductivity, matric potential, and water retention (via Clapp-Hornberger pedotransfer from clay/sand) alter infiltration capacity and thus Hortonian/Dunne runoff
How soil moisture profiles and water-table/drainage response change with texture
Relative sensitivity of QRUNOFF, QOVER, QDRAI, and QRECHARGE to clay fraction
not_answerable: Absolute field-validated recharge rates for any specific real aquifer (this is an idealized controlled experiment)
Effects of soil structure, macropores, or preferential flow (ELM uses matrix-flow Richards/CLM hydrology, not dual-porosity)
3D lateral groundwater flow interactions (single-column has no lateral connectivity)
Reactive/geochemical transport unless PFLOTRAN coupling is explicitly enabled

parsed.n_justification: One column per clay level spanning 5% to 55% in 10% increments (5,15,25,35,45,55) provides an evenly sampled sensitivity curve of runoff/recharge partitioning while keeping the ensemble minimal and interpretable; sand fraction is co-adjusted to conserve mass (silt held constant) so only clay is the controlled variable.
assumptions: All columns share the same site (US-ARM, SGP Oklahoma), PFT, topography (hillslope/fdrai), and CLMNCEP forcing; only %clay (with compensating %sand) is varied.
Silt fraction held at 50% (40% only for the 55%-clay case where sand is floored at 5%) so clay is the primary controlled gradient.
A separate ~200-year accelerated-decomposition + final spinup precedes the 15-yr production run so each column reaches hydrologic quasi-equilibrium before analysis.

Soil hydraulic parameters (Ksat, saturated matric potential, porosity, b-exponent) are derived internally via ELM's Clapp-Hornberger/Cosby pedotransfer functions from the prescribed sand/clay, which is the mechanism linking texture to partitioning.
SIMULATOR (Richards-equation soil hydrology) is ELM default; PFLOTRAN coupling is not required for this water-partitioning question and is left off.
Recharge is diagnosed from QDRAI/QRECHARGE (bottom drainage to unconfined aquifer) and runoff from QOVER+QDRAI-free surface term; partitioning ratio computed as multi-year means.
